extraction.name: VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling
extraction.description: A paper proposing VideoChat-Flash, a video multimodal large language model for long-context video modeling using hierarchical video token compression (HiCo), a multi-stage short-to-long training scheme, the LongVid dataset, and a Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack benchmark.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid was constructed by leveraging existing datasets and curation steps: the authors used high-quality short video captions and event-level annotations from multiple sources, filtered consecutive segments that could be regrouped into long video sequences, generated dense event labels with timestamps, and constructed long video QA pairs from captions, event labels, and timestamps. For the MH-NIAH-Video benchmark, images were sourced from MS-COCO using its human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LongVid is curated from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. The paper also mentions using MS-COCO images for the Multi-Hop Needle-in-a-Video-Haystack benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filtered consecutive segments that could be regrouped into a long video sequence, concatenated captions to form dense captions, extracted major events from captions using an LLM for some datasets, and generated event labels with corresponding timestamps and QA pairs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For LongVid, consecutive video segments were filtered and regrouped into long video sequences; short video captions were used directly when available; dense captions were formed by concatenating lower-level captions; event labels were extracted or directly reused depending on annotation quality; long video QA pairs were then constructed from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Dense event labels were generated for each long video. Existing high-quality event-level annotations were directly used when available. For other datasets, the major event was extracted from captions using an LLM. Long video QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps. For MH-NIAH-Video, MS-COCO human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs were used.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: An LLM was used to extract the major event from captions; captions were also recaptioned using AI models such as VideoChat2, Gemini, and LLava-NeXT-34B in the training data pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that long video models face challenges from high redundancy and that compression can cause loss of detailed information. It also states that some long video models may perform worse than image-based MLLMs on certain benchmarks. For NIAH-Video, the paper notes possible information leakage and limited discrimination, motivating the new multi-hop benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation for long-context video modeling. LongVid is used for instruction tuning and multi-stage short-to-long learning; the Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack benchmark is used for evaluation of long video context understanding and reasoning.
